services.name: Perennials grown on our benches
services.blurb: Salvias, yarrow and penstemon potted here and kept outside for weeks before they go on sale.

services.name: California native plants
services.blurb: Manzanita, ceanothus and coffeeberry started from local stock, ready for the fall planting window.

services.name: Shrubs for clay and deer
services.blurb: Gallon and five-gallon shrubs that put up with heavy clay and the deer that visit at night.

services.name: Trees, bare-root and potted
services.blurb: Bare-root fruit trees in January, potted shade and native oaks the rest of the year.

services.name: Vegetable and herb starts
services.blurb: Tomato, pepper and herb starts hardened off outdoors so they do not sulk after planting.

services.name: Annuals and hanging baskets
services.blurb: Spring and fall color in flats and baskets, planted up here and grown on before sale.

services.name: Soil, compost and mulch
services.blurb: Compost and planting mix by the bag or yard, with advice on how much to work into clay.

services.name: Delivery and planting
services.blurb: We bring the plants on a flatbed and plant them at the depth and spacing on your list.

services.name: Garden advice at the bench
services.blurb: Bring a leaf, photo or soil sample and a grower tells you what is going on.

proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: Every salvia I ever bought at a big store keeled over by July. Inez told me theirs sit outside on the bench for at least six weeks first. I planted eight last October in Sebastopol clay and all eight came back this spring.
reviews.name: Marguerite O.

reviews.text: We lost most of the yard in the fire and had no idea where to start. They sat with a sketch of our lot, picked natives that keep their distance from the house, and delivered them in two loads.
reviews.name: Ignacio F.

reviews.text: Bought two bare-root apple trees in January. The grower showed me how to soak them, where to cut back, and how deep to set the graft. Both leafed out in April.
reviews.name: Wren D.

reviews.text: Deer were eating everything along our fence. I brought in a chewed branch and got a list of shrubs they mostly leave alone. Six months in, one nibble on a currant, nothing else.
reviews.name: Bodhi S.

reviews.text: The tomato starts were shorter than the ones at the grocery store, which worried me. Turns out that is what being grown outside looks like. They took off in the raised beds.
reviews.name: Lacey T.

reviews.text: Small thing, but someone looked at a photo of my yellowing camellia on a Sunday afternoon and told me it was the drip line, not a disease. Saved me a bottle of spray I did not need.
reviews.name: Philippa M.

proof.guarantee: Any perennial or shrub from our benches that dies in its first year, bring back the tag and we replace it.
